surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Mammoth end the Wild’s 15-game point streak
paras: Lawson Crouse struck first for the Mammoth early in the first. There were five goals in the second period alone. Jack McBain and Michael McCarron opened the second period with a fight, and Logan Cooley made it 2-0 for the Mammoth on the power play early in the period. Liam O'Brien and Nick Foligno dropped the gloves early in the period. Bobby Brink got the Wild on the board on the power play early in the period, and Dmitri Simashev pushed the lead to 3-1, 44 seconds later. Blake Coleman cut Utah’s lead to 3-2 less than two minutes later. Dylan Guenther made it 4-2 for the Mammoth with 49 seconds left in the second, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Coleman struck again with just over four minutes left to pull the Wild within one.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Karel Vejmelka made 22 saves for the Mammoth, and Jesper Wallstedt stopped 17 of 21 at the other end.

Joel Eriksson Ek took four penalties on his own. The officials called 14 penalties, a total the league sees about once every 40 games. The Mammoth improved to 13-10-3, seventh in the Central, while the Wild dropped to 18-4-5, tied for first in the NHL in points.

items.text: The Wild’s 15-game point streak is over.
Jonas Brodin passed Mikael Granlund for seventh on the Wild’s all-time assists list, with 225.
Mikhail Sergachev extended his point streak against Minnesota to seven games.
